featured_reviews.name: Amrita Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Came across this place by chance as it is situated in a bylane not easily visible. The Google reviews made me tempted to try it and I am glad to have visited this place.

The mandeli fry was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft of the inside. The taste of the coating was excellent and the combo with the green chutney and onion was superb 👌 A must try for appetizer!

Malvani prawns gravy was excellent too. It had a balanced spice level, and the prawns size and quantity was sufficient for 2 people. A must try!

The rice bhakri we had with the prawns needs a special mention, as it was super soft and thin unlike those thick and dry bhakris very common in many places.

The prawns pulav too was good in taste, and needs to be tried with a fish gravy to enjoy the combination.

A warm and cozy place, with the ambience trying to match the cuisine they serve, this place is a must try for those looking for home-cooked, freshly prepared Maharashtrian-style seafood cuisine.

While the preparation does take some time, but it is worth the wait, as we know it is being freshly prepared.
Those unwilling to wait can call and order in advance.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur
featured_reviews.review_text:
This restaurant, located near Ghatkopar bus depot on Link Road and close to the Eastern Express Highway.

Since we was traveling around we decided to give a try but it turned to disappointment. Don't fall into the trap of its appearance. At first, the photos, high review count, and name may convince you, but it's a big NO. The hotel management is not malvani. The owner was unavailable, and the staff, who were not Maharashtrian, struggled to understand some things. There was lot of negative reviews about poor service and rude behavior from staff, but we didn't experience any such issues. They were good, albeit lacking some services, like not providing a finger bowl. The place was empty, with no waiting time. Although four AC units were installed, with three of them on, it still felt hot.

Now, about the taste - we ordered multiple dishes (see pictures), but they didn't meet expectations. Except for the 'Banjara kebab' and 'tandoori lollipop', I didn't enjoy much else. The 'bombil fry' was good but overpriced. They should add two more pieces for rate they added. The 'chicken fry' dish was the worst, containing bones instead of being boneless. Avoid it at all costs. The 'manchow soup' was just okay, and the 'prawns fry' wasn't impressive either. The thalis we tried - crab, king surmai, and special chicken - were below average.

The ambiance was more than okay, but the biggest reason to avoid this place is its pricey menu. We've tried many Malvani restaurants, but this one's rates were almost 1.5 times higher, without justifying the taste.

The final verdict is to avoid it if you crave good taste, all my 6 family members were unhappy and lastly, the restaurant should focus on reducing rates.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Food was good and ambience was not that happening. It has only 1 AC hall which was not big enough and thus few tables for dining.

The options are aplenty: right from Tisriya Sukha, to Prawns sukke, to Surmai Masala and even Baby Sharks. However, if you’re one with an appetite, they also serve the best seafood thalis, which are just as delicious!

As you can imagine, this is home-style dining at its finest and Malvan katta not catering to anyone’s tastes but he and his family’s so expect hearty, coconut-y flavours and plenty of masala spices.
The menu’s filled.

featured_reviews.name: Rishabh Kushwaha
featured_reviews.review_text:

We tried a variety of fish thalis, and the taste and quality were excellent and truly commendable. The food felt fresh, flavorful, and homely. The prices are very reasonable, especially for thalis, biryani, and other menu items.

featured_reviews.name: foodie_namz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today had been to Maharashtra Lunch home to try their Veg thali. The place was very nice and welcoming.
The thali included soft phulkas served with a well-spiced dry Baigan sabzi and a flavourful aloo mutter gravy. The yellow dal and rice were comforting.
It was accompanied by fresh onion salad, crispy roasted papad, sol kadhi which enhanced the overall taste and variety on the platter. The gulab jamun served at the end was warm and perfectly sweet, making for a delightful finish.

A wholesome and well-balanced meal for anyone looking to enjoy a traditional Indian thali with homely flavours.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
Authentic Seafood Soul Food in Vikhroli!

If you are craving a proper Maharashtrian seafood feast, this place is a gem. We recently tried their Pomfret Thali, and it was an absolute delight.

The Pomfret: The star of the show. We had both the Pomfret Fry and the Pomfret Curry. The fry was perfectly crisp on the outside with a flavorful masala coating, while the fish remained juicy inside. The curry had that authentic coastal tang and spice balance that pairs so well with rice.

The Rice: They serve Indrayani Rice, which is a game-changer. It’s sticky, aromatic, and has that homely feel that elevates the entire meal.

Accompaniments: The thali comes with Bhakri, which was soft and fresh—perfect for soaking up the curry.

Vibe: It’s a classic "lunch home" setup—clean, no-frills, and focused entirely on the quality of the food. Great for a hearty weekend lunch.

Rating: 4.5/5
Must try: Pomfret Thali with Indrayani Rice.

featured_reviews.name: Maharashtrian traveller
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Delightful Dining Experience

We visited the **Maharashtrian Lunch Home – Vikhroli branch**, and the dining experience was exceptional, offering rich flavors and a thoughtfully curated ambiance. The atmosphere was calm, cozy, and elegantly designed, with walls decorated with sketches of Maharashtrian village life that added a beautiful cultural touch.

For those unsure about what to order, the staff is attentive and helpful—do ask for their recommendations.

The **Surmai Thali** was a standout, featuring fresh, perfectly cooked fish with authentic coastal flavors. Each element in the thali complemented the other, making it a satisfying and wholesome meal.

The **Chicken Thali** was equally impressive, with tender, well-marinated chicken prepared in flavorful gravy, paired with well-balanced sides. The portion size was adequate for one person and quite fulfilling.

While the pricing is slightly on the higher side, the quality of food and the peaceful ambiance make it worth it.

This restaurant is a great choice for anyone looking to enjoy authentic flavors in a relaxed setting.

Food: 5 | Service: 5 | Atmosphere: 5

featured_reviews.name: Ahmad
featured_reviews.review_text: Soulful and Authentic Maharashtrian Feast ! If you are looking for a meal that tastes like home, this Veg Thali is a winner. I especially loved the Indrayani Bhaat - it’s rare to find such fragrant, traditional rice in a standard thali. The Dahi Kanda adds a refreshing crunch to balance the flavors. Great portions and truly satisfying. Highly recommended !

Malvan Samudra

Honest Review!
Malvan Samudra is one of the oldest restaurants in Vikhroli (West) specially known for its authentic sea food and Indian food. It's taste was great especially it's sea food. Good Ambiance and you can visit here with family and friends. They serve Malvan cuisine as well as chinese and others. The specialty is Bombil chilly. I also ordered bheja fry. It was awesome. But when we visited the last time the results were disappointing and the taste was not good as always. We ordered Chicken Handi and ended up regretting because first of all the prices were too high and chicken handi was eventually tasteless, it was not even spicy , no salt was added to it. Before main course we ordered Chicken Crispy too but it's taste was average. With chicken we ordered wade and bhakris they we good as it doesn't need anything miracle to make good bhakris and wade. We expected main course to be tasty but it wasn't. But still if you are willing to visit this place you should take a chance. Surely try their Solkadhi with main course and they vary with many fish thalis and chicken thalis.
Eat Fresh Stay Healthy ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Ankeet D
featured_reviews.review_text:
TAT turned out to be such a delightful surprise. The location is absolutely stunning, the interiors are tasteful and upscale without trying too hard, and the staff is pleasant and attentive. But the real star here is the food — delicious, refreshingly different, and crafted for people who genuinely enjoy exploring new flavours.

What I loved most is that they don’t go overboard with “high-tech” gimmicks. They keep the basics intact, honouring the soul of good food — something that has become rare these days.

And yes… the desserts deserve their own applause. The phirni and kulfi were simply outstanding.

A definite must-try!

featured_reviews.name: Ruch
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited TAT, Vikhroli and it turned out to be such a pleasant surprise

The place has a really warm, coastal-inspired vibe with subtle detailing that makes the whole dining experience feel calm and elevated — perfect for long dinners or catching up with your people.

Coming to the food this is where they really shine 🌊🍽️
Their coastal menu is super well-curated with a focus on fresh seafood, balanced flavours and great presentation. Everything feels thoughtfully made and not overdone, which is honestly refreshing.

Tried a few dishes and the flavours were on point especially if you enjoy coastal and regional Indian cuisine. It’s one of those places where you can actually taste the authenticity in every dish.

Overall
A great spot if you’re looking for good food + calm ambience + something different from the usual Mumbai dining scene. Definitely a place I’d revisit, especially for seafood lovers!

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!

featured_reviews.name: Yogen Sachdev
featured_reviews.review_text:
I finally revisited Maaslli – Saraswat and GSB Speciality last night for my annual catch-up with friends, and once again, it reminded me why this place is rightly awarded the best seafood restaurant in Mumbai.

We started off with their seafood soup, which was practically a treasure hunt in a bowl, packed with so many varieties of seafood that I stopped trying to count after a few spoonfuls. A rich, flavorful start that set the tone for the evening.

Next came the Bombil Fry, and let me say this: if you visit Maaslli and skip this, you’re missing the highlight of the menu. Perfectly crisp on the outside, melt-in-your-mouth inside, it was unanimously the table favorite.

The Prawns Ghee Roast, their signature dish, followed, aromatic, buttery, and spicy in all the right ways. You could taste the freshness of the prawns through the layers of ghee and masala.

I ordered the cucumber mint cooler as a palette cleanser, one of the best non-alcoholic drinks I’ve had. Truly impressed by the bar at this outlet

To round things off, we indulged in the Crab Gravy with Bhakri, a true coastal comfort combination. The gravy had that home-style depth of flavor that only comes from slow cooking and authentic spices.

Between the impeccable flavors, warm service, and the nostalgic coastal touch in every dish, Maaslli continues to set the gold standard for seafood in Mumbai. Can’t wait for next year’s reunion, though honestly, I might not wait that long to go back.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Maaslli Restaurant & Bar, at Kemps Corner, Mumbai.
Basically a Sea food Restaurant, but also have other non veg dishes on their platter.
One cannot afford to miss the fried Bombil (Fresh, Fried Bombay Ducks).
They have a great Menu.
They do have various Thali dishes and other alcarte dishes.
It is just mouth watering and thus unable to put in words to describe the dishes.
One must enjoy the crab dishes and crab soup.
They also present you their fresh catch and you may select the fish if your choice, depending upon the weight the rate is fixed.
The atmosphere is damn cool and decent with fishes reflecting in the walls and partisans.
The curry, different types is served and we are asked to taste, then by adding coconut oil again to try. Thus if you are ordering any curry dish you can select your choice of curry.
The staff is very courteous and friendly.
The person, Mr. Anthony, accepting the order is very polite and well versed with the description of the dishes.
Service is quite fast and dishes are very tempting.
The complete crockery is if copper OR may be brass (not sure). But it is a real experience to have your food in such dish and even the fork and spoon.
The soup was something different from the normal ones which all must have experienced.
Crab soup, very tasty and hot enough and goes without saying very tasty.
Sweet dish of Modak and a sweetening dish made if milk and sprinkled with pista, woh! Lovely.
The dishes are well place and economically rated.
If you are in that area, do give a try and taste the tasty dishes, yes! Definitely one have a inclination and a taste for Sea Food.
The Bar is open and you have choices of hard drinks, Cocktails and even Mocktails.
A seperate Menu displaying the drinks is maintained.
Do visit, you will not regret nor your pockets will be pinched.
Enjoy the Sea Food and friendly service.

featured_reviews.name: Danish Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food Review: A Major Disappointment
​I truly believe one shouldn't speak ill of food, but I had an absolutely terrible experience here.
​We ordered the Prawns Koliwada and Crispy Chicken. Given the massive hype surrounding this restaurant, we expected the food to be exceptional. As a seafood lover—especially prawns fry—I was genuinely shocked from the very first bite. The Prawns Koliwada was completely tasteless; the spice profile was missing and there was no salt at all.
​To make matters worse, when my wife cut into a prawn, we realized they hadn't been cleaned properly. The digestive tracks (veins) were still inside. Every single prawn was like that, which completely ruined our appetite. On top of that, the dish was incredibly expensive.

​The Crispy Chicken
​The second dish was just as bad. It was so sour that after just one bite, we had to ask the waiter to pack it up. Neither my wife nor my kids could eat it—it was a total waste of money. I’ve had Crispy Chicken at many places, but this was the worst. Honestly, the local Chinese joint in my neighborhood makes it better.

​The Lesson Learned
​This experience taught me one thing: don't just rush to a restaurant based on an influencer's video. You have to check real reviews first. I have no idea what people actually like about the food there. My wife and I are beyond disappointed.

Ordered a chicken thali with wade and Chicken sukka with wade...
The preparation was nice, similar to what I ate 3 or more decades back...total bill was Rs 900...
The thali had: 4 big wades, sufficient rice for one(I shared and we probably left some) a small wati of sol kadi(used to be yummy but not so much this time) a chutney which was fantabulous before but it was just alrite this time...no vegetable or any other filler...

Will I visit again, doubtful because nothing appealed so much that it would be worth the 4hour travel from residence to Mumbai...
I loved their fish curry from the past era, not sure if it's the same...

name: Konkani Haven Isvara
description: Experience the essence of Konkan at Isvara, where cherished childhood memories of indulging in authentic Konkan cuisine come to life. Founder Megha Datwani's vision is to recreate the warmth and tradition of village holidays, paying homage to the flavours that evoke the spirit of the Konkan community. Each dish at Isvara narrates a tale of tradition and passion, from mouth-watering seafood to fragrant spices like kokum and jackfruit. Chef Arun Jadhav brings these treasured recipes to life, inviting guests to savour the essence of Konkan culture with every bite. Step into Isvara's serene ambience, where natural elements and inviting aromas transport you to a quaint Konkan village.

featured_reviews.name: Kiran Rajput
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Kokani Haven with a friend as I was craving seafood. It was a bit tricky to find since it’s inside Poco Loco restaurant, but we managed after a few minutes.

The place was crowded, so service took some time, but the food was worth it. We ordered butter garlic prawns, pomfret curry, sol kadi, and rice bhakri. Everything was delicious, though the bhakri was a bit stiff even after requesting a softer one.

Special thanks to Phurba, who was warm, kind, and attentive throughout. The great food and welcoming vibe made it a wonderful experience!

featured_reviews.name: Imtiyaz Mohammad
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have seen one cloud kitchen serving multiple brands but this is the first time I witnessed a dine in restaurant serving two labels. One is the konkani haven isvara and the other is Poco Loco or something like that.

Every customer, including us, walks in with a puzzled face and asks, ye konkani place kidhar hai. Definitely some work needed on signages.

Food was good but a couple of points to note here :-

The prep time for the dish is on the higher end compared to the standard. Just something for you to know and plan

Secondly, i found it expensive based on where we ate and what we ate.

featured_reviews.name: Taronish Mullan
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place could have surely been better. The non veg food was quite good and fresh but the veg food was very disappointing. Firstly Konkani food doesn’t mean that kari patta HAS TO ADDED. Each dish can have different flavours. The Prawn rava fry and the Surmai fry both were lovely. The Prawn curry was a bit sweetish. The vades were the best. They really need to improve on the veg food. He suggested Dry paneer chilly along with Ghavan like Neer dosa which was weird to have without gravy. For the main course I specifically asked if the drumstick dish was a curry since I wanted to have with rice. He said yes and then a dry dish came up. They really need to improve their service. It took forever to get simple dishes. Waiting for food was almost half hour or more .
Also found the price a bit steep
Btw- for those who don’t know Poco Loco and Konkani Haven in chowpatty is in the same restaurant.

featured_reviews.review_text: We visited their Huges Road branch and we were disappointed with everything. We ordered Ghavan with fish curry, but what they served was actually neer dosa and not ghavan. Service is too slow, they need to improve overall. featured_reviews.name: sachin moghe
featured_reviews.review_text:
last week happened to be in the area. had read numerous reviews about this restaurant as one of the best in girgaon hence dropped by for lunch.
location is excellent. near to charni road station (e). right on a traffic intersection. cannot miss.
place is very small and cramped. each table is meant to accomodate four but the seats are so small that only two can sit comfortably, one on either side. the restaurant was being attended by only one wait staff hence service as delayed.
i had ordered chicken sukka thali with tandoori roti. thali had two rotis, chi sukka, gravy, solkadhi and kanda nimbu. chicken was ordinary, large pieces about 4-5 but more of bone and very little meat. the masala was very spicy quite unlike manglori masala which is coconutty and flavourful. the gravy which came along with thali was ok. I was given another bowl of gravy alongwith rice. the waiter specifically asked me to have this gravy alongwith rice. this gravy was so spicy that my entire mouth was on fire. I had to leave half the rice uneaten. solkadhi was good. I wanted to order a glass but due to bad experience with other items in the thali, did not order solkadhi again.
there is nothing manglori about solkadhi hence don't understand why do manglori restaurants serve solkadhi. I won't be surprised if tomorrow these people say that solkadhi is originally a manglori dish.
hopeless place. the person sitting in front of me was having fish fry thali and the expression on his face clearly indicated that he too was disappointed.
bad place. could be ignored. there is nothing modern about this place. there are many better places than this one nearby. while walking from charni road metro to this place I passed by panshikar ahar which is truly iconic. after finishing my lunch or rather half eaten lunch i regretted my decision to enter this place.
